source.version: Published journal article, The Annals of Statistics 52(5), 2024, pp. 2217–2240; registered 24-AOS2433-1.pdf

enumeration.method: Independent small-cap heading enumeration and visual comparison of all four complete theorem statements.

checks: Four complete main-text Theorems, numbered 2.1–2.4. Theorem 2.2 spans pages 5–6 with eleven centering terms, eight additive variance terms and full auxiliary matrix/kernel definitions. Independent small-cap heading enumeration excludes proof headings, citations and Lemma 2.5.

Nineteen entries and ten supporting passages preserve the exact linear inverse-correlation model, pooled covariance, sample correlation, unpenalized estimator, iid fourth-moment assumption, distinct sample/population B, full CLT normalizers, fitted precision and null/alternative test statistics.

Independent reconstruction confirms 33 direct uses and 49 related connections. T2.3–T2.4 inherit T2.2 assumptions without acquiring its contrast-specific nu, sigma, D0 or D1. T2.4 replaces H0 by H1 and uses population rather than estimated normalizers.

The later Discussion explicitly supplies bounded correlation spectral norm for T2.3–T2.4, finite active K and inclusion of the true basis set. Those passages are preserved separately from the original theorem wording. Conditions for simplified power comparisons are not inserted into the full theorem.

Thirteen source issues remain explicit: theta-hat reuse for raw/corrected/penalized fits, implicit inverse and scale existence, the y=1 singularity, arbitrary zero contrast, trace powers, a.s. versus proof o_p wording, n scaling and local-alternative ambiguity. No source statement is repaired or proof certified.

Every entry retains literal source terms, source kind and heading, and source-backed selectors. All 49 related theorem connections have explicit paper-local paths and explanations; reused notation does not merge distinct definitions.

All six content JSON artifacts reproduce byte for byte using the seven saved per-paper scripts. Frozen hashes, source-specific formula checks, independent heading enumeration, reconstructed dependency graph and schema validation pass.

source_notes.note: The symbol B first denotes p^-1 tr(Rhat A_k Rhat A_l), then denotes the population trace matrix plus the y correction in Theorem 2.2. Local entries D6 and D10 preserve distinct meanings.

Theta-hat is the unpenalized B^-1 b estimator in T2.1–T2.2. The text calls its bias correction the final estimate, then reuses theta-hat for penalized estimation. T2.3 retains shrinkage c and its proof uses the raw asymptotic coefficient behavior. No unconditional extension to penalized/corrected fits is asserted by this census.

The source uses sample and population B inverses, inverse sample diagonal square roots, and inverse/diagonal normalization of Rhat_L without explicit nondegeneracy, eigenvalue bounds or fitted positive-definiteness guarantees. Known symmetric bases alone do not guarantee these operations are defined.

The preceding assumption only requires a finite y=p/(n-2) limit; Theorem 2.2 contains (1−y)^-2, singular at y=1. Retain the formula and record the missing explicit exclusion rather than replacing its denominator.

Theorem 2.2 quantifies over any constants pi_1,...,pi_K, including the zero contrast, but normalizes by sigma^-1. No sigma>0 or variance nondegeneracy is explicitly stated. Preserve the quantifier and flag this limitation.

The quadratic loss and variance contain trace/matrix powers whose placement matters. In particular Theorem 2.2 prints both tr[(RD1)^2] and tr(RD1)^2. Equation (5) additionally prints min rather than argmin and a trace/scalar-minus-identity expression. All are retained without repair.
Theorem 2.1 states almost sure convergence, whereas the displayed proof establishes an o_p(1) expansion. The census preserves the theorem assertion and does not claim proof verification.
Equation (2) contains n; (7) omits it despite the substitution description. T_n is retained without n, and theorem normalizations use nT_n exactly as printed.

Theorem 2.4 invokes T2.3 conditions while explicitly replacing H0 by H1. It does not assume both. The condition inheritance does not import T2.2 contrast-specific conclusion, nu or sigma into the null/alternative tests.

The Discussion explicitly says T2.3–T2.4 require bounded population-correlation spectral norm, although their printed statements do not spell it out. Record that as a separate source condition D19; do not rewrite the quoted statements.

The full T2.4 prints H1 without a local-signal rate. Delta_n=o(1), sample proportion and trace conditions are introduced later for simplified power comparisons; the Discussion calls the alternative local. Preserve both the printed theorem and this scope ambiguity.

Known exact basis representation and finite active K are part of the theory. Growing candidate sets and selection in simulations do not establish a theorem for an arbitrary growing active K or model misspecification.

The motivating normal approximation whitens the sample-mean difference but prints an unwhitened mean vector in its Gaussian mean. This is archived as source context, not used to alter theorem statements.

ambient_resolution.T2.1: D1–D6 give the common-covariance samples, pooled S, R and D decomposition, known symmetric linear inverse-correlation model, sample correlation and unpenalized estimator. D7 supplies y_n−2 and finite y. D8 is the printed standardized iid-coordinate fourth-moment model. K is finite in the theory per A6–A7. No regularized estimator is substituted; a.s. wording is preserved despite proof o_p notation.
ambient_resolution.T2.2: Inherits T2.1 assumptions and adds D9 trace boundedness. The coefficient estimator remains D6. D10 is the new population B; D12 builds D1 from its inverse and the arbitrary contrast pi. D11 supplies beta_w, D0 and g; D13 gives the complete nu and sigma². D and D0/D1, sample/population B and trace powers remain distinct. Zero contrast, y=1 and invertibility issues remain explicit.
ambient_resolution.T2.3: Inherits the T2.2 assumptions, including trace boundedness and the exact coefficient model, but not its contrast-specific conclusion. D14–D15 form the fitted precision and T_n. D16 supplies population mu0, sigma0² and A0; D17 supplies plug-in Rtilde and estimated normalizers; c-hat=1/(1+p/(n−2)) is local. D19 records the later explicit bounded-spectral-norm condition. H0 is the null; raw-versus-corrected/penalized fit scope remains flagged.
ambient_resolution.T2.4: Inherits the common T2.3 assumptions with H1 replacing H0. D15 is T_n, D16 its population null mean/variance, D18 supplies population c and Mahalanobis delta_n. The full power formula uses Phi and Phi(−z_alpha)=alpha; no estimated normalizer occurs in the printed limit. D19 retains the Discussion spectral requirement. Additional Section 2.3 local-signal and trace conditions A4–A5 are not silently inserted into the statement.

source_claim_references.scope: Inherit the population model, fourth moment, finite aspect ratio and underlying exact linear estimator setting.
Inherit assumptions, not the arbitrary contrast, coefficient-CLT centering nu or scale sigma.
Retain common assumptions and population normalizers; replace H0 by H1, and use population c rather than c-hat.
Trace convergence lemma is used in the proof; not a statement dependency.
Proof is deferred, but the entire theorem and all of its auxiliary formulas are printed in the main text. No supplement body read.

review_limits: Published journal PDF registered as 24-AOS2433-1.pdf, pinned by hash and its ScholarSphere download URL.
Supplementary and appendix bodies excluded. Penalties and HBIC are named externally; no theorem for arbitrary penalized fits is inferred.
Source and schema validation do not certify mathematical proofs or repair source ambiguities.
